omd-locale-handoff.label: oh-my-design locale handoff
omd-locale-handoff.activation: Use the installed $omd:locale-adapter skill first: treat KO as canonical, lock every protected fact and literal before editing, and adapt EN, JA, ZH-CN, and ZH-TW as independent product copy rather than sentence-aligned translations. Then use the installed $omd:humanize skill in VERIFY mode across all five locales. In this task, VERIFY means comparing protected facts, locale terminology, register, and repeated copy signals; it does not authorize writing verification software or rebuilding the browser environment. Preserve the command, numbers, DESIGN.md, product capabilities, and interaction contract exactly; reject cross-locale terminology, unsupported claims, and edits that merely make every locale share the same English information order. During static source inspection, audit every flex/grid control row that can wrap: its vertical row gap must be at least as large as any border, underline, transform, or selection treatment extending to the control edge, so adjacent hit areas cannot overlap at 200% zoom. Also audit every overflow auto or scroll region that can contain clipped useful content: it must contain a reachable control or be an explicit keyboard focus target with visible focus-visible treatment, plus a useful accessible name when its content does not already provide one. Do not add unnecessary Tab stops to decorative or non-scrollable containers. Treat this as a 900-second delivery envelope: make the first product-file edit before 450 seconds, stop optional verification by 720 seconds, and begin the final response before 810 seconds. Do not run Chrome, Chromium, Playwright, browser-harness, screenshots, qlmanage, or any other direct browser or renderer command in this benchmark task. The external evaluator is the only browser acceptance authority. Use static source inspection and content comparison only; report browser proof as unresolved without attempting it. Never author verify.*, verifier.*, check.*, probe.*, a temporary shell program, CDP/browser automation, a DOM shim, a mock browser, or a new test runner.

omd-repair-harness.label: oh-my-design repair harness
omd-repair-harness.activation: Use the installed $omd:apply skill. First lock the current protected-contract ledger: every current control, row, form, disclosure, hook, state, and fact has allowed_delta 0 unless the original user prompt explicitly requests adding or removing it. Neither you nor a specialist may relax that ledger. Before editing, also lock a semantic_color_ledger for every current or planned meaningful foreground/background pair: token, surface, content type, and measured or unresolved contrast proof. If an accent-on-surface pair is unmeasured, never ship it as meaningful normal text; keep the label in the DESIGN.md ink/text-role token and preserve the accent only as an adjacent non-text dot, bar, ring, or icon. Do not invent a darker substitute, do not rely on color alone, and do not treat an unresolved disclosure as permission to keep the risky pair. Then use the Agent tool once for $omd-ux-writer and once for $omd-ux-engineer, in parallel when possible, and explicitly pass model: opus plus mode: bounded-repair-advisory to each call. Give each the identical immutable ledgers, only one or two named risk questions, at most three ranked findings, and about 300 words. Require each response to begin with one first_safe_edit containing an exact existing target, evidence, an acceptance-relevant smallest change, protected_contract_effect: none, and one acceptance check. When state/status/accent tokens exist, one engineer risk question must classify all planned semantic color pairs as normal text or non-text and identify every unmeasured pair before the main edit. Do not request general section audits, new controls, new FAQ items, or new facts. Specialists must not edit files; the main agent owns all product edits and rejects contract-drift advice. Treat this as a 900-second delivery envelope: make the first product-file edit before 450 seconds, stop optional verification by 720 seconds, and begin the final response before 810 seconds. Once both advisories arrive, apply one accepted first_safe_edit with a targeted Edit within 90 seconds and before any ledger recap, advisory summary, planning prose, full-file reread, or second analysis pass. If an existing snippet can be patched safely, do not make a whole-file Write the first transaction. The first transaction must be a real product change that advances the original acceptance criteria; never use whitespace, comments, timestamps, or same-value replacement to touch the clock. Any new unreviewed semantic pair uses the fail-closed ink-label plus non-text-accent default. The final same-route acceptance packet is a checklist and observed result, not an executable artifact; do not write a DOM shim or mock browser. Never author verify.*, verifier.*, check.*, probe.*, a temporary shell file, CDP/browser automation, or a new test runner, even when that program would launch a real browser. Use only repository-existing tests/evaluators or a direct browser command that writes no verification program. Attempt each browser/runtime verification mechanism once. If it is blocked, report browser proof as unresolved and deliver the finished product diff.
